resources.string: Copy text in any app, then find it here.
Your existing files have not been erased.
Tap to copy and return · Hold for options
Tap to copy · Hold for options
Start or restart Shizuku or a compatible service, then connect ClipHistory.
Start or restart Shizuku or a compatible service, then try again. Setup help explains what you need.
Tap Connect. If the prompt closes or never appears, open your service app, allow ClipHistory in its authorized apps, then return and tap Connect.
Allow ClipHistory in your service app’s authorised applications.
Your saved history is still available. Start your service to record new copies.
Check your service and the recorder diagnostics, then try again.
Your service app is running in a mode ClipHistory can’t use. Start it with wireless debugging or ADB, then reconnect.
ClipHistory needs Shizuku API 13 or newer. Update your service app, restart it, then reconnect.
Your service app was started with root. Android only allows clipboard reading when the service is started with wireless debugging or ADB. Restart it that way, then reconnect.
ClipHistory works only on the main phone profile. Work profiles, private spaces and other users aren’t supported.
This Android version’s clipboard service isn’t supported yet. Copy the Diagnostics report and share it in a bug report.
Open your service app from the launcher, then return to ClipHistory.
Select the app you use to start your service. Run only one service at a time.
This entry is no longer available.
Connect the recorder to change saved history.
Lowering the limit deletes older entries.
This deletes all saved texts and their recovery copy. Gboard and your current Android clipboard are unchanged.
This replaces your current clipboard with harmless test text. Your saved history stays unchanged.
No test event was confirmed. Check your service and try again.
A clipboard event arrived, but storage verification failed.
This checks the connection now, not long-term background reliability.
This report contains no saved clipboard text.
Copy text as usual. Open ClipHistory and tap an entry to copy it back.

Unlock the phone and start your non-root service again if needed. Automatic recovery and Resume after reboot prepare the recorder when enabled. If it does not reconnect, open ClipHistory and tap Connect. Force stop and Stop recorder remain effective until you explicitly start again. Pause stays saved. Copies made while recording is stopped cannot be recovered.
History is encrypted on this device. There are no accounts, ads, analytics, or cloud sync. Text is readable in the app and Android clipboard while in use.

Text marked sensitive by its source app is skipped by default, for example passwords and copies from private browsing in some browsers. You can capture it in Settings → Privacy. Saved sensitive entries stay hidden in the list; use View to see one. Auto-delete defaults to 5 minutes; timed entries also expire after a reboot. It removes saved history, not Android’s clipboard. Turning capture off removes saved sensitive text. Not every app marks private text. Pause recording when needed.
Text only. Entries over 64 KiB are skipped. Only the main phone profile is supported.

Screenshots and screen recording are blocked by default. You can allow them in Settings → Privacy. Android 13 and newer also offer a separate Hide history in Recents control. On Android 11–12, blocking screenshots also hides Recents previews. Do not assume other apps mark every private copy as sensitive; Pause before copying private text.
Add Clipboard to Quick Settings for a small floating panel with your newest three texts. Settings also offers Open full history. The tile asks you to unlock before showing saved text.
You can also add it from Quick Settings → Edit.
Swipe down twice to open Quick Settings. Tap Edit (the pencil), then drag Clipboard into your active tiles. Close Quick Settings and open it again to use the tile.
Return to the previous app after copying from history. The quick panel always closes after a copy.
Turn off to stay in your history.
Android did not allow this copy. Your saved text is unchanged.
Check the current history before trying again. View diagnostics for details.
